name: Suez Canal
genZNote: One container ship got stuck sideways in the Suez Canal for six days in 2021 and it held up an estimated tens of billions of dollars of trade a day — that's how much rides on this one canal.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: An artificial, man-made canal in Egypt — not a natural strait — connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
Opened in 1869, it removed the need to sail around the entire African continent to travel between Europe and Asia.
Owned and operated by Egypt through the Suez Canal Authority.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: One of the world's most important shipping shortcuts — a large share of global trade, including a significant portion of world container traffic and oil shipments, passes through it.
The main alternative when it's unavailable or congested is the much longer route around Africa's Cape of Good Hope, which adds significant time and fuel cost.
A 2021 blockage by a grounded container ship (the Ever Given) is a widely cited real-world example of how disruptive a Suez closure can be to global trade.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 India Connection
bullets: A meaningful share of India's trade with Europe moves through the Suez Canal, making it an important route for Indian exports and imports on the western side of the country.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Suez Canal is a man-made canal in Egypt connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, avoiding the long route around Africa.
keyFacts: Man-made canal, opened 1869, located in Egypt.
Connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
Alternative route when unavailable: around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.
2021 Ever Given grounding is a well-known real-world disruption example.
commonConfusion: The Suez Canal is a CANAL (man-made), not a strait — straits like Bab-el-Mandeb and Hormuz are naturally occurring channels.

highYieldFacts: Suez Canal: man-made, opened 1869, Egypt, connects Mediterranean ↔ Red Sea.
Alternative when blocked: Cape of Good Hope route around Africa.
2021 Ever Given incident is a frequently cited exam example of chokepoint disruption.
commonTraps: Canal vs. strait: Suez and Panama are canals (built); Hormuz, Malacca, Bab-el-Mandeb, Bosporus, Dardanelles are straits (natural).
mustRemember: Suez Canal = Egypt's man-made Mediterranean-Red Sea shortcut, critical for Europe-Asia trade.
